newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso firmer on strong jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso firmer on strong jobs data.

text.p: The Mexican peso extended early firmness at late morning trade on Thursday after lower than expected employment data encouraged investors to switch from dollars to the peso instruments.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart were 2.5 and 2.7 percent firmer, respectively, at 7.8525/7.8550 and 7.8455/7.8480 per dollar.

Mexico's Statistics Institute (INEGI) announced the open unemployment rate for June was 3.4 percent, down from 3.9 percent in May and well below an average forecast rate of 3.92 percent in the latest Reuters survey of 12 Mexico City financial firms.
Same-day peso contracts had meanwhile closed trade for the day 7.6 centavos firmer at 7.8455/7.8490 per dollar.
